| **Textbook** | [Volume I: Introduction to Machine Learning Systems](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol1/) |
| **Prerequisites** | Python, linear algebra, basic calculus, and introductory probability |
| **Format** | A 16-week semester or a 10-week quarter, with two 75-minute lectures per week |
| **Materials** | [Slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol1.html) · [Labs](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/) · [TinyTorch](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/) ([instructor guide](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/blob/dev/tinytorch/INSTRUCTOR.md) for autograding) · no GPUs needed |

## Description {#description}

Students study how data pipelines, training, optimization, and deployment work on a single machine with up to eight accelerators. Along the way they build a small deep learning framework, TinyTorch, one module at a time.

## Learning outcomes {#outcomes}

By the end of the course, students can:

- Build a small deep learning framework that trains a model.
- Measure where time and memory go in a training or inference workload.
- Choose optimizations, such as compression, against deployment constraints.
- Deploy and evaluate a model against latency, memory, and quality targets.

## Reading schedule {#schedule}

In the semester plan, students read one Volume I chapter each week; the quarter plan combines some weeks. Each chapter has a matching [lab](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/), and the first eleven weeks also have a [TinyTorch](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/) module. The instructor decides which labs and modules to assign.

## Assessment {#assessment}

A suggested split; each offering sets its own.

| Component | Weight |
|:---|:---|
| TinyTorch modules (8, auto-graded) | 35% |
| Lab Decision Logs (short written analyses) | 25% |
| Design challenges (the open-ended part of the labs) | 20% |
| Capstone: deploy one application on several hardware targets, with a design report | 20% |

## Suggested papers {#papers}

Optional readings that pair with the chapters.

| Week | Topic | Paper |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 4 | Data Engineering | Sambasivan et al., "Everyone Wants to Do the Model Work, Not the Data Work" (CHI 2021) |
| 7 | ML Frameworks | Chen et al., "TVM: An Automated End-to-End Optimizing Compiler" (OSDI 2018) |
| 10 | Model Compression | Dettmers et al., "LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale" (NeurIPS 2022) |
| 11 | HW Acceleration | Jouppi et al., "In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit" (ISCA 2017) |
| 13 | Model Serving | Yu et al., "Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Models" (OSDI 2022) |
| 14 | ML Operations | Sculley et al., "Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems" (NeurIPS 2015) |

## Adapting this syllabus {#adapting}

- Each offering sets its own dates, deadlines, and policies on late work, collaboration, and AI tools.
- **Two semesters:** this course leads into [Scaling Machine Learning Systems](scale-syllabus.qmd).
